info.title: Python TDD workflow with requirement-based code changes

parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

2: from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence

4: from amaranth.hdl import *
5: from amaranth.hdl.ast import ShapeCastable, ValueCastable

14: class Field:
15:     def __init__(self, shape, offset):
16:         try:
17:             Shape.cast(shape)
18:         except TypeError as e:
19:             raise TypeError("Field shape must be a shape-castable object, not {!r}"
20:                             .format(shape)) from e
21:         if not isinstance(offset, int) or offset < 0:
22:             raise TypeError("Field offset must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
23:                             .format(offset))
24:         self._shape  = shape
25:         self._offset = offset
26: 
27:     @property
28:     def shape(self):
29:         return self._shape
30: 
31:     @property
32:     def offset(self):
33:         return self._offset
34: 
35:     @property
36:     def width(self):
37:         return Shape.cast(self.shape).width
38: 
39:     def __eq__(self, other):
40:         return (isinstance(other, Field) and
41:                 Shape.cast(self._shape) == Shape.cast(other.shape) and
42:                 self._offset == other.offset)
43: 
44:     def __repr__(self):
45:         return f"Field({self._shape!r}, {self._offset})"
46:

48: class Layout(ShapeCastable, metaclass=ABCMeta):
49:     @staticmethod
50:     def cast(obj):
51:         """Cast a shape-castable object to a layout."""
52:         while isinstance(obj, ShapeCastable):
53:             if isinstance(obj, Layout):
54:                 return obj
55:             new_obj = obj.as_shape()
56:             if new_obj is obj:
57:                 break
58:             obj = new_obj
59:         Shape.cast(obj) # delegate non-layout-specific error handling to Shape
60:         raise TypeError("Object {!r} cannot be converted to a data layout"
61:                         .format(obj))
62: 
63:     @staticmethod
64:     def of(obj):
65:         """Extract the layout from a view."""
66:         if not isinstance(obj, View):
67:             raise TypeError("Object {!r} is not a data view"
68:                             .format(obj))
69:         return obj._View__orig_layout
70: 
71:     @abstractmethod
72:     def __iter__(self):
73:         """Iterate the layout, yielding ``(key, field)`` pairs. Keys may be strings or integers."""
74: 
75:     @abstractmethod
76:     def __getitem__(self, key):
77:         """Retrieve the :class:`Field` associated with the ``key``, or raise ``KeyError``."""
78: 
79:     size = abstractproperty()
80:     """The number of bits in the representation defined by the layout."""
81: 
82:     def as_shape(self):
83:         """Convert the representation defined by the layout to an unsigned :class:`Shape`."""
84:         return unsigned(self.size)
85: 
86:     def __eq__(self, other):
87:         """Compare the layout with another.
88: 
89:         Two layouts are equal if they have the same size and the same fields under the same names.
90:         The order of the fields is not considered.
91:         """
92:         while isinstance(other, ShapeCastable) and not isinstance(other, Layout):
93:             new_other = other.as_shape()
94:             if new_other is other:
95:                 break
96:             other = new_other
97:         return (isinstance(other, Layout) and self.size == other.size and
98:                 dict(iter(self)) == dict(iter(other)))
99: 
100:     def _convert_to_int(self, value):
101:         """Convert ``value``, which may be a dict or an array of field values, to an integer using
102:         the representation defined by this layout.
103: 
104:         This method is private because Amaranth does not currently have a concept of
105:         a constant initializer; this requires an RFC. It will be renamed or removed
106:         in a future version.
107:         """
108:         if isinstance(value, Mapping):
109:             # Special handling for UnionLayout - check that at most one field is specified
110:             if isinstance(self, UnionLayout) and len(value) > 1:
111:                 raise ValueError("Initializer for at most one field can be provided for a union "
112:                                 "layout (specified: {})"
113:                                 .format(", ".join(sorted(value.keys()))))
114:             iterator = value.items()
115:         elif isinstance(value, Sequence):
116:             iterator = enumerate(value)
117:         else:
118:             raise TypeError("Layout initializer must be a mapping or a sequence, not {!r}"
119:                             .format(value))
120: 
121:         int_value = 0
122:         for key, key_value in iterator:
123:             field = self[key]
124:             if isinstance(field.shape, Layout):
125:                 # For nested layouts, recursively convert the nested values
126:                 if isinstance(key_value, Mapping) or isinstance(key_value, Sequence):
127:                     key_value = field.shape._convert_to_int(key_value)
128:                 else:
129:                     # If it's not a mapping or sequence, treat as a scalar value
130:                     key_value = key_value
131:             try:
132:                 # Handle ShapeCastable objects that have custom const methods
133:                 if isinstance(field.shape, ShapeCastable) and hasattr(field.shape, 'const'):
134:                     const_value = field.shape.const(key_value)
135:                 else:
136:                     const_value = Const(key_value, Shape.cast(field.shape))
137:                 int_value |= const_value.value << field.offset
138:             except TypeError as e:
139:                 raise TypeError("Reset value must be a constant-castable expression, not {!r}"
140:                                 .format(key_value)) from e
141:         return int_value
142: 
143:     def __call__(self, target):
144:         """Create a View from this layout and a target value."""
145:         return View(self, target)

148: class StructLayout(Layout):
149:     def __init__(self, members):
150:         self.members = members
151: 
152:     @property
153:     def members(self):
154:         return {key: field.shape for key, field in self._fields.items()}
155: 
156:     @members.setter
157:     def members(self, members):
158:         offset = 0
159:         self._fields = {}
160:         if not isinstance(members, Mapping):
161:             raise TypeError("Struct layout members must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
162:                             .format(members))
163:         for key, shape in members.items():
164:             if not isinstance(key, str):
165:                 raise TypeError("Struct layout member name must be a string, not {!r}"
166:                                 .format(key))
167:             try:
168:                 cast_shape = Shape.cast(shape)
169:             except TypeError as e:
170:                 raise TypeError("Struct layout member shape must be a shape-castable object, "
171:                                 "not {!r}"
172:                                 .format(shape)) from e
173:             self._fields[key] = Field(shape, offset)
174:             offset += cast_shape.width
175: 
176:     def __iter__(self):
177:         return iter(self._fields.items())
178: 
179:     def __getitem__(self, key):
180:         return self._fields[key]
181: 
182:     @property
183:     def size(self):
184:         return max((field.offset + field.width for field in self._fields.values()), default=0)
185: 
186:     def __repr__(self):
187:         return f"StructLayout({self.members!r})"
188: 
189:     def const(self, value):
190:         """Create a constant value from this layout and a value."""
191:         if value is None:
192:             return Const(0, self.size)
193:         return Const(self._convert_to_int(value), self.size)

197:     def __init__(self, members):

199: 
200:     @property
201:     def members(self):
202:         return {key: field.shape for key, field in self._fields.items()}
203: 
204:     @members.setter
205:     def members(self, members):
206:         self._fields = {}
207:         if not isinstance(members, Mapping):
208:             raise TypeError("Union layout members must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
209:                             .format(members))
210:         for key, shape in members.items():
211:             if not isinstance(key, str):
212:                 raise TypeError("Union layout member name must be a string, not {!r}"
213:                                 .format(key))

215:                 cast_shape = Shape.cast(shape)

221: 
222:     def __iter__(self):
223:         return iter(self._fields.items())
224: 
225:     def __getitem__(self, key):

227:

229:     def size(self):
230:         return max((field.width for field in self._fields.values()), default=0)

235:     def const(self, value):

239:                 raise ValueError("Initializer for at most one field can be provided for a union "

255:                 return Const(0, self.size)

296:     def __iter__(self):
297:         offset = 0
298:         for index in range(self._length):

300:             offset += Shape.cast(self._elem_shape).width
301: 
302:     def __getitem__(self, key):
303:         if isinstance(key, int):
304:             if key not in range(-self._length, self._length):

306:                 raise KeyError(key)
307:             if key < 0:
308:                 key += self._length
309:             return Field(self._elem_shape, key * Shape.cast(self._elem_shape).width)

311: 
312:     @property
313:     def size(self):

320: class FlexibleLayout(Layout):
321:     def __init__(self, size, fields):
322:         self.size   = size
323:         self.fields = fields
324: 
325:     @property
326:     def size(self):
327:         return self._size
328: 
329:     @size.setter
330:     def size(self, size):
331:         if not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
332:             raise TypeError("Flexible layout size must be a non-negative integer, not {!r}"
333:                             .format(size))
334:         if hasattr(self, "_fields") and self._fields:
335:             endmost_name, endmost_field = max(self._fields.items(),
336:                 key=lambda pair: pair[1].offset + pair[1].width)
337:             if endmost_field.offset + endmost_field.width > size:
338:                 raise ValueError("Flexible layout size {} does not cover the field '{}', which "
339:                                  "ends at bit {}"
340:                                  .format(size, endmost_name,
341:                                          endmost_field.offset + endmost_field.width))
342:         self._size = size
343: 
344:     @property
345:     def fields(self):
346:         return {**self._fields}
347: 
348:     @fields.setter
349:     def fields(self, fields):
350:         self._fields = {}
351:         if not isinstance(fields, Mapping):
352:             raise TypeError("Flexible layout fields must be provided as a mapping, not {!r}"
353:                             .format(fields))
354:         for key, field in fields.items():
355:             if not isinstance(key, (int, str)) or (isinstance(key, int) and key < 0):
356:                 raise TypeError("Flexible layout field name must be a non-negative integer or "
357:                                 "a string, not {!r}"
358:                                 .format(key))
359:             if not isinstance(field, Field):
360:                 raise TypeError("Flexible layout field value must be a Field instance, not {!r}"
361:                                 .format(field))
362:             if field.offset + field.width > self._size:
363:                 raise ValueError("Flexible layout field '{}' ends at bit {}, exceeding "
364:                                  "the size of {} bit(s)"
365:                                  .format(key, field.offset + field.width, self._size))
366:             self._fields[key] = field
367: 
368:     def __iter__(self):
369:         return iter(self._fields.items())
